Solve a model for one or more subjects

Source: R/solve.R
pmx_ode_solve.Rd

Runs model over the event table events with the parameters params, and returns the compartments and the model's outputs at every observation record. Nothing is drawn at random: this is the deterministic core that the population simulation builds on.

Usage

pmx_ode_solve(model, events, params = double())

Arguments

model

A model from pmx_ode_model().

events

An event table: from pmx_ode_events(), or a NONMEM-style data frame with columns ID, TIME, EVID, AMT, CMT, RATE, DUR, II, ADDL and SS (any case; all but TIME optional). Columns named like a model parameter are covariates, each record carrying its value.

params

The model's parameters, a named numeric vector. A covariate column of events takes the place of its parameter.

Value

A data frame with id, time, one column per compartment and one per model output, one row per observation record.

Errors

pmx_ode_error_events for a record that breaks a rule of the event table, naming the row; pmx_ode_error_argument for a parameter with no value; pmx_ode_error_solver for a closed-form model whose rate constants are not positive.

Warnings

pmx_ode_warning_solver when the solver fails for a subject: that subject's outputs are NA from where it failed, and the others are solved (design §8). pmx_ode_warning_steady_state when a steady state of a model with no closed form does not converge.

Examples

m <- pmx_ode_model({
  cl <- exp(tcl); v <- exp(tv); ka <- exp(tka)
  cp <- linCmt()
})
ev <- pmx_ode_events(amt = 100, ii = 24, addl = 6, cmt = "depot",
                     time = seq(0, 168, by = 12))
head(pmx_ode_solve(m, ev, params = c(tcl = 0, tv = 3, tka = -0.7)))
#>   id time       depot  central cl        v        ka       cp

#> 2  1   12   0.2582432 60.86565  1 20.08554 0.4965853 3.030322
#> 3  1   24 100.0006669 33.64642  1 20.08554 0.4965853 1.675157
#> 4  1   36   0.2582449 79.37885  1 20.08554 0.4965853 3.952040
#> 5  1   48 100.0006669 43.83267  1 20.08554 0.4965853 2.182300
